There was a good layer of leaf mold on the ground here when I bought the property, mostly due to lack of any kind of maintenance. I raked it up and incorporated it into two beds, with compost and pea gravel. The difference is significant. For example, the bed that just got compost and mulch when I built it has a 2 year old apricot that is about 1.5 feet tall. The bed with leaf mold, compost, and mulch has a 2 year old apricot that is 4 feet high. Elderberries without are about 2 foot, with at above 6 foot. Echinacea without about 2 foot and haven't flowered, with about 3 foot and flowered heavily. Sage though, performs worse with leaf mold. Without is 1 foot high and flowered the first year. With is half a foot, has not flowered, and is barely holding on. It also greatly increases soil water retention. I almost never water the beds that had leaf mold added, vs monthly watering for the beds that don't.

Hugel mounds are mostly meant to form a raised bed. Breaking it up into much smaller sections performs the same task, it's just harder to recognize where they are. I have wood buried everywhere, especially in drought prone areas that I don't feel like watering. It is effective, just harder to manage.
